research_question: After a five-second peer-majority displacement with aligned taker flow, does a causally estimated lagging market retain a costed beta-implied fair-value gap at the next one-second executable price?

hypothesis.economic_cause: Information is incorporated asynchronously across related perpetual markets. A majority peer displacement can establish a temporary equilibrium change before the lagging market has fully repriced.
hypothesis.causal_sequence: Prior one-hour beta and correlation -> completed five-second peer displacement -> aligned peer taker flow -> follower underreaction -> frozen peer-implied target -> next-second executable entry -> local two-bar micro-pivot invalidation.
hypothesis.market_structure_mapping: Cross-market displacement creates an intermarket fair-value gap. The target is the peer-implied equilibrium frozen at confirmation, not a fitted fixed reward multiple.
hypothesis.cost_and_ordering: Next-second open plus two adverse ticks, taker entry, maker target, taker stop, two additional adverse stop ticks, stop-first ordering if target and stop occur in the same second.
hypothesis.forbidden_changes: No threshold grid, no future beta, no same-bar entry, no target extension, no follower-confirmation delay, no account-performance claim from this diagnostic.

dataset.source: Binance public USD-M daily aggregate trades
dataset.visibility: aggregate-trade timestamp floored to second plus one second

decision_rule.pass: Implement the unchanged detector in NautilusTrader, freeze fresh non-overlapping weeks before data, and enforce the project account/risk/execution contracts.
decision_rule.fail: Reject the second-scale cross-asset gap mechanism. Do not tune G1-G3 thresholds or horizons.
